articles.title: Haydock tips: Big Mojo fancied to retain Sprint Cup crown
articles.summary: Ahead of another busy Saturday of action, Kate Tracey is joined on the Weekend Winners panel by Callum Helliwell and Declan Rix; in this week's episode, the team take aim at Haydock, paying particular attention to the feature Sprint Cup
articles.body:
Eight runners are set to go in challenging conditions, with the ground expected to be heavy for this six-furlong dash.

Almeraq heads the market as he aims to bounce back from disappointment in the July Cup, while Wathnan duo Kind Of Blue and Paborus also take their chance. Marvelman and Coppull represent Andrew Balding and Clive Cox respectively, and last year's winner Big Mojo returns to defend his crown.

"I'm with the favourite Almeraq . He's a wonderful horse who I think deserves an awful lot of credit after that horror fall he took at York - it was a proper mother-and-a-father fall. To come back and win on his first start in the Cathedral Stakes, it was like someone had said a prayer for him.

"Not only did he win the Cathedral, he then went to Royal Ascot and won the QEII Jubilee. Tom Marquand said he felt a bit claustrophobic, but I love that he sustains his runs and has a good attitude.

"He has a good, strong shoulder and I think he'll handle the ground. He's got plenty of form in his career on soft, whether he'll handle heavy ground - we'll see. I think you can completely forgive him the July Cup form as it was his first time going down a hill and the field broke, leaving him caught on a wing. He ran too keen, got no cover and the ground was too quick for him.

"If he runs like any of the horses the William Haggas team ran at Haydock on Thursday, he's going to go very close as they're in great order."

"I absolutely love Marvelman in this - bring on the rain! I want it to be an absolute bog by the time Marvelman gets there. We're going to have another day of racing before then!

In the Park Stakes on September 13 last year it was a great birthday present for Callum, as it he absolutely gagged up.

He ran a mighty race last time, having them all off it from a long way home when finishing third in top-class company. Keep the rain coming!"

"I'm going to be with Big Mojo to repeat the feat from last year. I thought 9/1 was a fair price - although not as big as last year when he took full advantage of the draw bias. He has a similar draw this time so I'm hoping it will come to the fore.

Three runs ago he finished eight at Royal Ascot in the Group 1 King Charles III Stakes, not being beaten far whatsoever. Admittedly he was in the right group that day when the bias came to the fore and improved from his reappearance at York.

The July Cup was no good for him, he looked a nightmare that day. He was so keen and was hanging but it was much more like it at the Curragh last time, getting back to winning ways in a Group 3. Hopefully that's the confidence booster he needs.

articles.title: Daryz warms up for Arc with dominant display in Prix Foy
articles.summary: Daryz was given the perfect rehearsal ahead of his bid to retain his crown in the Prix de l'Arc de Triomphe with a smooth success in the Prix Foy at Parislongchamp
articles.body:
Francis-Henri Graffard's charge made the perfect start to his four-year-old campaign by winning two more Group Ones at his beloved ParisLongchamp, with a comeback victory in the Prix Ganay followed by a runaway triumph in the Prix Aga Khan IV.

He could only finish third when sent across the Channel for the Prince of Wales's Stakes at Royal Ascot in June, but with connections feeling they had viable excuses for that below-par run, the son of Sea The Stars was expected to regain winning ways back on home turf.

On paper his task was not entirely straightforward, with George Scott's 10-length Coronation Cup winner and fellow Arc aspirant Bay City Roller among his three rivals, and as expected the latter was sent straight to the front by Oisin Murphy in an attempt to draw the sting out of Daryz's exceptional finishing kick.

But Mickael Barzalona always looked ultra-confident in the saddle aboard the red-hot favourite, who cruised alongside Bay City Roller a furlong out and only had to be pushed out hands and heels to win by a length and three-quarters.

"I couldn't be happier with the trial he had today. We got a good lead and luckily Oisin made the pace a little bit harder at the top of the hill, so the horse was really travelling nicely," Graffard told Sky Sports Racing.

"For me as a trainer it was the best preparation I could have for the horse. He will come on a lot for that, I left plenty in him, so he should be spot-on for four weeks' time."

Scott too was delighted with the performance of the runner-up and is hoping for rain in Paris ahead of a rematch with Daryz in Europe's premier middle-distance contest on October 4.

He said: "Oisin was very happy with him and we'll be hoping for a different set of circumstances in a month's time.

"We know that this horse has a high level of form on ground like this, but when it rains he's a different animal.

"He came here and travelled well, went through the race very well and got beaten by a better horse on the day. In four weeks' time that might be the case (again), but it might not, so we'll see.

"I think he's the best version of himself now. The winner might be as well, but in four weeks' time it's going to be completely different.

"He's going to be an underdog coming back, of course he is - Daryz is a champion and he is unbelievable around here. It was all perfect for him today and set up great, but I was very happy with our horse, Oisin was most happy, so we're looking forward to it."

Avec Toi made to work hard to stay unbeaten in Prix la Rochette

Hot favourite Avec Toi was made to pull out all the stops to maintain his unbeaten record in the Qatar Prix la Rochette at ParisLongchamp.

Christopher Head's colt had been hugely impressive in winning his first three starts and was long odds-on to make it four from four in this Group Three contest.

Imperial Strike, winner of his two previous starts for Andre and Lavinia Fabre, made a real race of it and there was little to choose between the pair in the dying strides, but Avec Toi was a short head in front at the line.

A likely rematch between the front two will take place in the Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere in four weeks' time.

Head told Sky Sports Racing: "It was a very nice race with five nice horses. I respected Imperial Strike from the beginning, so I'm very happy our horse won the race and we discovered there's a very nice horse to beat next time too!

"He's a very nice horse and he's done a great job today. It was a pretty tactical race and we are all happy.

"There is a lot to do between the two races and I'm very happy with that."

Ed Bethell's British raider Rogue Passion flashed home to claim Group Two honours in the Qatar Prix d'Aumale.

The Sioux Nation filly faced a significant step up in class having opened her account at the third time of asking at Carlisle three weeks ago.

Francis-Henri Graffard's Amusingly looked likely to win comfortably after travelling powerfully into the lead under Colin Keane, but Rossa Ryan produced Rogue Passion with a well-timed challenge to get up and claim victory.

Bethell told the Press Association: "We were hoping that she'd run a big race, she's a very nice filly who I've got a lot of time for.

"Obviously you don't know what you're taking on with the French horses, but she quickened up like a decent filly over the mile there and we're delighted."

When asked whether she would return to Paris for the Prix Marcel Boussac next month, the trainer added: "It's a conversation that needs to be had with the guys at Rogues Gallery (owners) because she needs to be supplemented if we're going to do it.

"We'll let the dust settle today, enjoy it and have the conversation in a few days' time. She's got options, but now she's a Group Two winner we want to try and get a Group One if we can.

"Today definitely was not unexpected. She's always shown she's a nice filly and it's a huge credit to the Rogues Gallery and Henry Lascelles who bought her."

articles.title: Spanish GP: Kimi Antonelli edges Ferrari in Madrid practice as Arvid Lindblad suffers first F1 crash at challenging Madring circuit
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli fastest from Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton in Practice Two; Arvid Lindblad first F1 driver to crash at new Madrid track; watch Spanish GP Qualifying from the all-new Madring circuit live on Sky Sports F1 at 3pm on Saturday
articles.body:
After being outpaced by his Mercedes team-mate George Russell in the day's first session, Antonelli produced a quicker time of 1:33.662 in Practice Two to edge out Ferrari duo Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton by little more than a tenth of a second.

The timesheet was further evidence of Antonelli's sky-high confidence, which was elevated by a stunning victory at the Italian Grand Prix last weekend as he won his home race from 19th on the grid to move 66 points clear of Russell at the top of the standings with 10 rounds of the 2026 season remaining.

On the evidence of Friday's sessions, Mercedes and Ferrari are closely matched and could deliver an exciting pole contest in qualifying on Saturday, with huge excitement in the Spanish capital as F1 returns to the city for the first time since 1981.

Many had predicted a high number of red flags on Friday - and throughout the rest of the weekend - due to the tight and punishing nature of a circuit that the field have never raced at before.

While there were several crashes and red flags in Friday's F2 and F3 sessions, the F1 drivers showed their excellence to avoid any major incidents in first practice, but it was Lindblad who came unstuck just beyond the halfway point of Practice Two.

The 19-year-old was driving impressively and had just elevated himself to fourth when he pushed too hard on his next flying lap, losing control at Turn 13 and spinning into the barrier at high speed.

Lindblad said: "It's not an easy track. We are all pushing to find the limits. It's new for all of us. Just made a bit of a mistake and overdid it in Turn 13. A shame. I apologise to the mechanics and the team. It's extra work for them tonight.

"But looking at the big picture, it's been a good day. We are very fast. I was running P4 on merit and was only two tenths from P1 which is really strong.

"A lot of confidence in the team going into tomorrow. I'm just focused on resetting and trying to block it out and taking all the good learnings."

A delay of just over 10 minutes put an end to the qualifying simulations that had been taking place at that stage, securing Antonelli's position at the top of the timesheet.

Russell was fifth after appearing to struggle to optimise his setup, but still managed to edge out Red Bull's Max Verstappen and McLaren's Oscar Piastri.

"It was fun to drive the track for the first time," Russell said. "It's always a great experience driving a new circuit.

"FP1 was a strong session. FP2 we made some setup changes which weren't quite as good, so we will probably revert back on that. So far so good."

Reigning world champion Lando Norris was unable to set a time after a gearbox failure took him out of the session after just two laps.

McLaren were expected to be competitive in Madrid given Norris had claimed back-to-back victories before Antonelli's win in Monza, but there was little evidence of that on Friday.

While Norris has generally been quicker than Piastri recently, losing an entire session at a new circuit will put the Brit on the back foot going into Saturday.

articles.title: Saúde no DF: candidatos prometem novos hospitais e fim das filas | G1
articles.standfirst: Entre as propostas, estão um segundo hospital na Ceilândia, além de unidade no Guará, São Sebastião e outro entre Goiás e DF; candidatos falaram ainda sobre mutirões na saúde.
articles.summary: Candidatos ao governo do DF propõem a construção de unidades de saúde e mutirões para zerar as filas de cirurgias e exames na rede pública regional.
articles.body:
Imagem urna eletrônica — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

A semana de agenda dos candidatos ao governo do Distrito Federal começou com promessas para a saúde.

Em debates e reuniões nesta segunda-feira (21), os representantes prometeram a construção de novos hospitais em Ceilândia, Guará, São Sebastião e uma unidade entre Goiás e DF, além de um hospital do câncer.

Entre as propostas estiveram também a realização de mutirões em colaboração com o governo federal e contratação de especialistas.

O candidato do PT ao governo do DF, Leandro Grass, se reuniu com uma cooperativa de economia e crédito mútuo dos servidores do DF.

Grass ouviu as demandas da categoria, entre elas, reclamações sobre a falta de crédito para os servidores. A recuperação do Banco de Brasília (BRB) também esteve entre os assuntos discutidos.

O representante destacou um compromisso com as cooperativas de crédito para busca de fomento assegurado no plano de governo.

Ele disse ainda que vai recuperar o BRB, com diálogos com o Fundo Garantidor de Crédito e com o Banco Central, tratando tudo com transparência e planejamento. Grass disse que o BRB vai voltar a ser o banco para o qual foi criado: fortalecendo a economia do DF.

Na saída do encontro, Grass falou sobre a saúde pública.

"A gente vai criar um grande mutirão para tirar o povo da fila da saúde. Um mutirão de cirurgias, exames, trazendo também aqui especialistas. A partir do programa 'Agora Tem Especialistas', do governo federal, ampliando também os leitos, fazendo um mutirão de cirurgia de madrugada, final de semana, e tirar o povo da fila. E ao mesmo tempo, garantir a saúde perto de casa, com mais unidades básicas, equipes de saúde da família, prevenindo a doença", declarou.

A candidata à reeleição, Celina Leão (PP), começou o dia na Administração Regional do Gama, onde assinou ordens de serviço para obras no Gama e na Ponte Alta. Os recursos serão destinados à recuperação de vias, construção de novos parquinhos, pontos de encontro comunitários, e reformas de quadras poliesportivas e praças.

Se reeleita, Celina prometeu seguir com os investimentos em infraestrutura. Afirmou ainda que a expansão do metrô até o Gama vai diminuir o tempo de deslocamento de quem mora na região e trabalha no Plano Piloto.

Na área da saúde, prometeu construir um hospital de referência entre Goiás e o DF.

"A ideia é a gente fazer um grande hospital de referência aqui entre Goiás e o Distrito Federal, mantido pelos dois estados, porque hoje 50% dos partos aqui são do estado de Goiás. A demanda aqui do estado de Goiás sufoca muito o Hospital do Gama, porque a alta complexidade acontece toda aqui. Então a gente tá pensando em um outro hospital de forma integrada. É aquilo que eu quero conversar, se for eleita, com o novo governador do estado de Goiás, qualquer que seja, para que a gente faça ali um hospital integrado, porque aí tenho condição de pensar em reformar ou fazer um novo hospital para o Gama", afirmou.

Ainda no Gama, Celina fez uma visita ao "Instituto PAS", que oferece acolhimento para pessoas com transtorno do espectro autista.

O candidato Ricardo Cappelli, do PSB, esteve pela manhã na Rodoviária do Plano Piloto. Ele se apresentou aos passageiros, entregou panfletos e falou sobre propostas para o DF.

Cappelli afirmou que pegou um ônibus de Planaltina até o local e que, no trajeto, ouviu as demandas da população. O trajeto, segundo o candidato, durou cerca de 1h30.

Na saúde, o candidato apontou a falta de profissionais nas UPAs e nos hospitais. Ele afirmou que, se for eleito, vai contratar médicos logo na primeira semana de governo. Cappelli propôs ainda o programa Fila Zero, para zerar as filas de consultas, exames e cirurgias.

Ele também aproveitou para narrar a demora enfrentada pelos passageiros e defendeu faixa exclusiva e BRT para atender os moradores da área norte do DF.

"Chega aqui [na Rodoviária do Plano], as pessoas ainda pegam outro ônibus para ir ao trabalho. Se tivesse faixa exclusiva, ônibus expresso e faixa exclusiva de Planaltina para cá, a pessoa viria em muito menos tempo. O ônibus vem parando e lotado. É por isso que estou defendendo ônibus expresso em faixa exclusiva e BRT para Planaltina, Arapoanga e Sobradinho", defendeu.

Kiko Caputo, do Novo, participou de um debate em uma emissora de TV no início da tarde. Após o evento, ele seguiu para a Rodoviária do Plano Piloto, onde entregou panfletos e parou para conversar com passageiros e comerciantes.

O candidato afirmou que sua prioridade absoluta vai ser a saúde. Prometeu contratar mais médicos, enfermeiros, dentistas e profissionais de todas as especialidades.

Kiko afirmou ainda que vai ampliar o horário de funcionamento das Unidades Básicas de Saúde durante a semana e aos fins de semana e que vai implantar a telemedicina na rede pública para garantir a assistência à saúde 24 horas.

O candidato do Partido Novo defendeu ainda a construção de quatro novos hospitais no DF. Unidades seriam em São Sebastião, Guará e um segundo em Ceilândia, além do Hospital do Câncer.

"Eu, que perdi meus pais com essa doença, sei que cada dia é fundamental para a possibilidade de cura. Aí, quando a gente construir o segundo hospital da Ceilândia, aquele hospital antigo nós vamos reformar e vai ser o Primeiro Hospital da Mulher do DF. Quando construirmos o hospital do Guará, o antigo hospital vai ser reformado. E aí vai ser a primeira Clínica do Idoso para cuidar da longevidade. O Guará é onde reunimos a maior população de idosos do DF."

O candidato do Agir, Elisson Ferreira, se reuniu de manhã com representantes de uma organização de saúde mental. No encontro, ele assinou uma carta-compromisso que reúne propostas de prevenção, ampliação e fortalecimento da Rede de Atenção Psicossocial, financiamento dos serviços, atuação nas escolas e expansão dos CAPS e CAPSi.

Em seguida, o candidato também se reuniu com representantes do Observatório Social de Brasília e recebeu mais uma carta-compromisso. O documento reúne propostas de diversas áreas, como saúde, responsabilidade fiscal, meio ambiente e mobilidade.

Na área da saúde, um dos pontos apresentados é a transparência das filas de consultas e cirurgias. Elison destacou que esse é um desafio urgente e que será prioridade em seu eventual governo.

“Hoje, principalmente, a gente precisa resolver a questão da saúde. Tenho falado que até dia 21 de abril de 2027 a pessoa que está lá com exame marcado, com a sua consulta marcada, ela vai realizar sua consulta, porque nosso plano de governo prevê uma saúde digital, integrada e fazendo com que o cidadão de bem seja atendido”, afirmou.

À tarde, os candidatos José Roberto Arruda ( PSD ) e Paula Belmonte ( PSDB ) só tiveram um compromisso na agenda: um debate em uma emissora de TV. Pela noite, os dois participam de debate no Sindicato dos Professores, no SIG.

articles.title: Azerbaijan GP: McLaren predict four-way battle for victory with rivals in Baku after confirming more upgrades to MCL40
articles.summary: McLaren have shown strong recent form with Lando Norris claiming three pole positions and two race victories across the last four rounds; watch every session of the Azerbaijan GP from Thursday live on Sky Sports F1, with the race on Saturday at 12pm
articles.body:
After failing to claim a victory in the first 10 grands prix of the season, the reigning constructors' champions have come into form, with Lando Norris claiming three pole positions at the last four races and only being denied a third win by the unfortunate timing of a virtual safety car last time out in Madrid.

McLaren have once more exhibited strength in development, with regular upgrades brought to the MCL40 having played a significant part in catapulting them back into contention for victories.

The team's official preview for this weekend's race in Baku, which takes place on Saturday rather than the usual Sunday slot, revealed there will be new parts, and that their rotating 'H-Wing' will return to the car after not being used in Madrid.

"As part of the team's continued journey throughout the 2026 season, the team will bring to Baku a set of upgrades aimed to improve the aerodynamic performance of the MCL40," the team said.

"Additionally the H-Wing, that debuted in Monza, will be back in action on a track where the drag reduction can be a factor.

"As has been the approach in previous races this season, all new parts will be evaluated throughout practice before the team makes final decisions regarding the MCL40's Qualifying and Grand Prix setup for the weekend."

McLaren chief technical officer and chief designer Rob Marshall explained the team are keen to continue their development push despite their title hopes being extremely thin, with Kimi Antonelli dominating the Drivers' Championship and his Mercedes team well clear in the constructors' standings.

"With regulatory continuity into next season and the competition at the front so close, our motivation to keep developing the car remains high," Marshall said.

"We must balance that with work on next year's car, but our immediate focus is on delivering more performance and fighting for more victories in 2026, while carrying forward everything we learn."

The Baku circuit, which features the longest straight on the F1 calendar alongside several slow corners, creates a challenge that Marshall expects to create entertaining competition between the top teams.

"Baku will provide another valuable test of the MCL40 across a very different range of characteristics," Marshall added.

"Energy management and deployment will be particularly important, as will tyre and brake management with the cars arriving at Turn 1 after the long straight with these areas relatively cold.

"Operationally, there is very little margin for error on a tight street circuit. A small mistake can lead to significant repairs, lost track time and resources being diverted away from performance, so confidence, precision and disciplined execution will be essential throughout the weekend.

"We expect any of the top four teams to be capable of winning in Baku, with the chasing pack also getting closer, and we hope to be firmly in the fight at the front."

articles.title: Llegan carreras de F1 más cortas
articles.standfirst: La Comisión de la F1 da luz verde a varios cambios ya para 2027
articles.summary: La Comisión de la F1 da luz verde a varios cambios ya para 2027
articles.body: La Comisión de la F1, reunida en Londres por tercera vez esta temporada y presidida por Nicolas Tombazis, su responsable técnico, y por Stefano Domenicali, su CEO, ha acordado unos cambios de los que se habían hablado, pero que, ahora, reciben luz verde definitiva. El más llamativo es que las carreras de F1 serán más cortas a partir de 2027. Se ha establecido que la distancia de carrera pase de los actuales 305 kilómetros a sólo 290 kilómetros el curso venidero. Según la FIA, esto supondrá una reducción "de dos o tres vueltas" en función del circuito. La causa de esta disminución se encuentra en el pacto al que llegaron los equipos, la FIA y la F1 respecto a los cambios que se realizarán en las unidades de potencia para 2027 y 2028. Poco a poco la parte de combustible irá ganando terreno a la eléctrica, hasta llegar al 60 por ciento frente al 40 en 2028. Esto hace que la parte térmica necesite más combustible. Se barajó poner depósitos más grandes, pero eso aumentaría el peso de unos monoplazas ya muy pesados, con lo que se decidió reducir las carreras. Otra variación aprobada es la referida a las interrupciones de una carrera por lluvia, accidente u otras circunstancias. Ahora, se fijará una hora límite, de forma anticipada y no habrá que esperar tres horas, como era hasta ahora. Eso sí, se mantiene que debe haber un máximo de dos horas seguidas de carrera. La Comisión sigue esa línea al permitir que los entrenamientos también se puedan alargar, aunque, en este caso, no se especifica ni cómo ni cuánto. Además, y de acuerdo con el dictamen de la comisión técnica, se decidió que ya no será necesaria una homologación de las cajas de cambio en 2027. Según la FIA, así se podrá "preservar la libertad de desarrollo de los proveedores".

articles.title: Formula 1 reduces maximum distance of races by 15km among changes for 2027
articles.summary: F1 announces the maximum race distance for grands prix will be reduced by 15km from 305km to 290km for the 2027 season.
articles.body:
Formula 1 has announced the maximum race distance for grands prix will be reduced by 15km from 305km (189.5 miles) to 290km (180.2 miles) for the 2027 season.

Grands prix are limited to a maximum of two hours of racing, but when there are interruptions caused by rain or accidents, a "hard stop time" will replace the current maximum three-hour duration to finish the event.

This will allow for greater flexibility to complete disrupted races.

A statement from governing body the FIA said: "These changes were introduced to ensure that the spectators have the best possible chance to enjoy a full race if disruptions occur."

The hard stop time will vary from race to race, depending on local conditions.

At night races, for example, there will be more flexibility to allow the race to run later than at a daytime race when there is a relatively early sunset.

The reduction in race distance has been introduced because the ratio of internal combustion to electrical power is changing from 53-47 this year to 58-42 next year, before becoming 60-40 in 2028.

This means that the cars will use more fuel, and that became a concern when it emerged that some teams wanted to carry their chassis over into next year to save money.

As the fuel tank is within the chassis and therefore its size could not be changed, this meant those teams might not have been able to finish grands prix with their existing fuel tanks.

Another change agreed at a meeting of the F1 Commission, a rule-making body composed of the teams, the FIA and commercial rights holder F1, was to introduce "greater flexibility to extend free practice sessions should they be interrupted".

Under current rules, the clock does not stop in practice sessions in the event of a red flag caused by an incident, unlike in qualifying and races when the competition is suspended.

articles.title: F1 Grand Prix distances set to be reduced for 2027 season along with introduction of 'hard stop' time on race days
articles.summary: Grand Prix distances will be reduced from 305km to 290km in 2027; the change is required due to the alteration of technical regulations for next season; watch every session of the Azerbaijan GP from Thursday live on Sky Sports F1, with the race on Saturday at 12pm
articles.body:
At a meeting of the F1 Commission in London on Monday, the sport's decision makers agreed to reduce Grand Prix distances from 305km to 290km, which corresponds to a reduction of two to three laps depending on the circuit.

The change is being made because fuel flow rates are being increased next season as part of measures the FIA are introducing to optimise the all-new regulations brought in at the start of 2026.

The FIA said: "In line with the refinements to the Power Unit regulations to be introduced in 2027 on fuel flow, a reduction in the total race distance from 305km to 290km was approved, corresponding to a reduction of two or three laps."

The decision must be approved by the World Motor Sport Council, but that is expected to be a formality.

The FIA also announced slight changes to protocols around races disrupted by rain or other factors, with a three-hour limit (including interruptions) from race to start to finish removed, but a "hard stop" time for the end of any racing activity to be introduced.

A limit of two hours of actual racing remains, with those decisions taken "to ensure that the spectators have the best possible chance to enjoy a full race if disruptions occur."

It was also confirmed that there will be "greater flexibility to extend Free Practice sessions should they be interrupted."

The current rules only allow for practice sessions to be extended on Sprint weekends, but such measures may now also be available on a regular schedule.

articles.summary: Bullins is pursing another opportunity within NASCAR, and so the No. 6 RFK Racing Ford will have a new crew chief for Kansas and beyond
articles.body:
There will be a change atop the No. 6 RFK Racing pit box of Brad Keselowski, with Jeremy Bullins parting ways with the organization. Bullins is set to take a new opportunity elsewhere in NASCAR, while Mike Skarbowski will take over crew chief duties for Keselowski from Kansas this weekend onwards.

"We're excited for Jeremy and his family as he embarks on a new opportunity," a statement RFK Racing read. "Jeremy has been a terrific teammate, leader, and vital member of our competition think tan. Not only has he been a trusted voice with the #6 team, but he's also brought great value to the garage in sharing strategic insights and historical perspective as we've crafted a shared vision for RFK Racing's on-track success.

Bullins, who spent the bulk of his career with Team Penske before joining RFK in 2025, has ten Cup wins as a crew chief. Half of those victories came with Keselowski when he was still the driver of the No. 2 Penske Ford. Bullins' most recent win came with Harrison Burton and the Wood Brothers at Daytona in the summer of 2024.

Skarbowski, who was listed as RFK's team manager, previously worked as an engineer at Trackhouse Racing. This will be his first experience as a crew chief at the Cup level.

articles.standfirst: En KTM saben que perderán al que dominará el Mundial en los próximos años y mientras disfrutan de él
articles.summary: En KTM saben que perderán al que dominará el Mundial en los próximos años y mientras disfrutan de él
articles.body: El box de KTM en el Red Bull Ring parecía el camarote de los hermanos Marx. Al ser la cita de casa estaba atestado de invitados, incluyendo su CEO, Gottfried Neumeister, el consejero Heinz Kinigardner, una delegación de Bajaj, los indios que pusieron el dinero para sacar a la empresa de la bancarrota, o hasta niños hijos de directivos de la firma de bebidas energéticas. En ese ambiente de paroxismo, el equipo celebraba con largos abrazos la victoria de Pedro Acosta, la primera en MotoGP y la primera de los centroeuropeos desde Tailandia 2022 con Miguel Oliveira. Los jefes estaban encantados. “Soy el hombre más feliz del mundo”, proclamaba Pit Beirer, el director de Motorsport de KTM. Es una emoción indescriptible que viene de lejos. Estamos hablando de los momentos realmente difíciles que atravesó KTM a finales de 2024 y también en 2025. Incluso entonces, nunca pensamos en rendirnos; nadie dudó y todos seguimos luchando. Incluso cuando surgió el siguiente problema, fue una pesadilla, y una vez más tuvimos que luchar todos juntos. Pero todos perseveramos. Hace apenas unas semanas, ni siquiera soñábamos con una victoria. Luego llegó el segundo puesto (Aragón), después otro podio (Misano), y ahora la victoria en casa”, explicaba. El ejecutivo ‘naranja’ no ocultaba su euforia. “La victoria de Pedro es mucho más que eso: KTM se ha recuperado de su crisis; es un regalo para toda la compañía. Lo que Pedro logró es indescriptible. La forma en que se recuperó de la situación del sábado demuestra la clase de piloto que es”, soltaba. Más frío, como buen finlandés, estaba Aki Ajo, el director del cuadro oficial de KTM, pero su emoción se notaba en sus palabras. Decía a MARCA que siempre tuvieron fe en que este triunfo llegaría. “Seguro que seguimos creyendo durante todo el tiempo, pero, por supuesto, durante el camino, hubo muchos desafíos que no nos dejaron el mejor sabor de boca, pero este verano fue muy duro para nosotros. Empezamos la temporada muy bien; luego, llegaron varias decepciones; más tarde los retos, también técnicos, por supuesto, durante el verano. Estoy más orgulloso y feliz por Pedro, porque él mantuvo la positividad y también se mantuvo apretando a todo el mundo; siempre está apretando a todo el mundo de una manera fuerte. Sabíamos que si seguíamos haciendo las cosas bien, todo llegaría. Él nos lo estaba demostrando todo el tiempo, siempre mejora y su adaptación a distintas cosas es increíble, con su habilidad y talento”, indicaba. El dirigente nórdico estuvo con Acosta en sus títulos de Moto3 y Moto2, es de los que mejor le conocen. Por eso sabe que el murciano tiene una manera de llevar la moto única. “Es un talento especial, tiene también un estilo especial, pero de lo que estoy más impresionado de los últimos doce meses, es cómo se ha adaptado a todo esto. Él era un poco negativo a finales del año pasado, pero el punto de inflexión fue en algún momento en mitad del verano y cómo ha empezado a mejorar desde entonces. Especialmente, cómo se ha adaptado a distintas situaciones y cosas de la moto, como un comportamiento diferente, por eso está a un nivel increíble. Él es realmente completo”, analizaba. Ajo era rotundo al ser cuestionado sobre si el Tiburón de Mazarrón ganará algún título cuando llegue a Ducati en 2027. “¿Luchar por el título? Seguro. Pedro, es, definitivamente, el tipo que llegará como una tormenta a los top en el futuro, en el Mundial. No hay ninguna duda. Mientras, tenemos que disfrutar con él, aún nos quedan unas carreras, siete, que son más con los Sprint, con lo que tenemos mucho para disfrutar y para lograr lo máximo que podamos”, soltaba gráficamente. Ahora, Acosta está a 72 puntos de Jorge Martín y en KTM ni quieren oír hablar de pelear por la corona, por mucho que Marc Márquez le incluya como candidato. “No hablo del título, sólo de disfrutar y hacer lo máximo que podamos; por eso es por lo que tenemos que luchar”, replicaba el veterano director de equipo.

articles.title: F1 title race: Why Azerbaijan-Malaysia-Singapore triple header will shape what rest of 2026 championship chase will look like
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli's chief rivals may have all but ruled themselves out of winning the title but the season's first triple header could provide unpredictable twists; watch every session of the Azerbaijan GP from Thursday live on Sky Sports F1, with the race on Saturday at 12pm
articles.body:
The race on the streets of Baku - which takes place on Saturday rather than the usual Sunday - was originally due to be a standalone event with the Singapore Grand Prix following on two weeks later.

But the moving of the Bahrain Grand Prix to Malaysia in the week between the two events has created the run of three successive race weeks, with two more triple headers scheduled to close out the 2026 season.

So what can we expect from this first Azerbaijan-Malaysia-Singapore triple and what will the world championship picture - which currently sees Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli holding a commanding lead - look like on the other side into mid-October?

Last chance saloon for Antonelli's challengers?

While Antonelli's victory last time out in Madrid was fortuitous thanks to the Virtual Safety Car timing that helped him and hindered McLaren's race-leading Lando Norris, the Mercedes driver was enjoying another strong weekend at F1's brand-new venue and was in position to capitalise on such a slice of luck.

That victory, Antonelli's eighth in 14 races this season, means he arrives in Baku with an 81-point lead at the top of the Drivers' Championship.

Since seeing his title advantage over team-mate George Russell cut to just 25 points at the British Grand Prix at the start of July, Antonelli's lead has increased in each of the last five race weekends to its current season-high total.

Russell remains Antonelli's closest challenger but he all but conceded his hopes of beating his team-mate to the crown after falling more than the equivalent of three races wins behind the Italian by finishing fifth at the Madring.

Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton had already effectively ruled himself out after the previous weekend's race at Monza, but was more certain in saying his title hopes were over after brake problems at the Madring saw him register his first DNF of the season.

Hamilton is now 101 points off the pace while fourth-placed Norris, the grid's in-form driver alongside Antonelli, saw his own deficit grow to 106 points on a weekend the reigning world champion was unlucky not to make it three wins in four.

All the championship cards appear firmly stacked in Antonelli's favour, not that the young Italian appears to carry the weight of being the clear title favourite particularly heavily.

The 20-year-old has continued to insist he is "not thinking about the championship" in every interview he is asked about it, a mantra that his team boss Toto Wolff says is genuine and the best one for his driver to adopt.

Yet time is obviously running out for any one of the would-be challengers to put a stunning run of form and results together over the final rounds to truly trouble him.

There is still time, though, and with 83 points up for grabs during this first triple header of rounds alone - 75 across the three grands prix and eight for the Singapore Sprint - Mercedes are right to remain cautious - for now.

But should Antonelli finish the Singapore weekend on October 11 with a similar or even increased lead compared to the 81-point one he holds now, then the odds on him not becoming the sport's youngest-ever world champion will become very long indeed, even with a maximum of six rounds (and 150 points) left to play for.

What challenges do the next three tracks present?

Kicking off this intense run into the autumn is the Baku City Circuit , a high-speed, wall-lined street track through the middle of Azerbaijan's capital that has often featured on lists of a season's most dramatic races during its first decade on the calendar.

Last year's race - and indeed weekend - certainly fell into that category after a qualifying session that featured a record six red flags and a race, won by Red Bull's Max Verstappen, which saw then-title favourite and points leader Oscar Piastri crash out within six corners. The McLaren driver had also hit the wall in qualifying.

Antonelli, who finished fourth on his F1 debut in Baku last season and took a podium in F2 the year before, will be hoping to avoid those pitfalls as this year's driver to catch on a circuit which Mercedes, like at Monza, are being tipped to be particularly strong.

"Baku is completely different [to Madrid]. Slow-speed corners, massive straights, a little bit lower downforce as a result for those long straights," Sky Sports F1's Nico Rosberg told The F1 Show podcast.

"Engine power is always going to favour Mercedes in that way. We saw it in Monza, so I think Mercedes has to be the big favourite.

"Max Verstappen was fast in Monza, so maybe Verstappen can be the surprise there."

Then, for the first time in nine years, it is on to Malaysia and a Sepang International Circuit that was always a favourite among drivers and fans during its original 1999-2017 run on the calendar.

Ten current drivers were on the grid when F1 last raced there (with Charles Leclerc driving for Sauber in 2017's Friday practice), while Alex Albon and Liam Lawson drove there in junior series.

Antonelli, Russell and Norris are among those whose only experiences of the sweeping layout will have come in the simulation world, although even F1's most sophisticated tools cannot reflect the level of heat and humidity that famously accompanies racing in tropical Sepang.

But oppressive conditions are what drivers are regularly used to anyway in neighbouring Singapore at the Marina Bay Street Circuit , which has certainly been the most physically demanding race of the season in recent times.

What will be new in Singapore this year, though, is that its schedule features the Sprint format for the first time. It will be the sixth and final Sprint weekend of the season.

Sprint weekends by their nature - with a single practice session before the competitive sessions begin - increase the chance of unpredictability and punish any early driver mistakes or missteps on car set-up. Marina Bay, with its omnipresent walls, will only heighten that challenge.

What impact will the latest upgrade packages have?

As has been the case throughout this first season of the sport's new-look cars, the upgrade packages the leading teams bring to each race weekend will continue to have an impact on the pecking order.

Much-improved McLaren will have another package of changes on their MCL40 for Baku, a track where they struggled last year irrespective of Piastri's travails.

Mercedes' long-awaited upgrade will arrive for the following race in Malaysia. The W17 has not been upgraded to any significant degree at a single race since the Canadian Grand Prix at the end of May, an approach which has certainly helped Ferrari, McLaren and Red Bull to catch up.

However, the big question - and, for their rivals, the potential worry - is how much the Silver Arrows' Sepang package pushes them on.

"I think we are bringing a solid upgrade in Malaysia," Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff told Sky Sports F1 in Madrid. "So we've got to survive another race in Baku. Let's see.

"Sometimes it doesn't correlate with the road so well, so I hope that it does and hopefully that puts us on par with the others in terms of upgrades, but you never know."

Mercedes also have an ADUO power-unit upgrade still to deploy this season should they wish, amid suggestions the Silver Arrows could deploy it to coincide with whatever race Russell takes his expected engine grid penalty at.

Ferrari - who continue to show flashes of impressive promise but too regularly trip themselves up - and Red Bull - who appear to be getting closer to a first win of the year with Verstappen - will likely have new parts too across the triple header before attention throughout the field fully switches towards the 2027 challengers.

Will Antonelli remain in realistic chasing distance for 2026's final races by then?

articles.title: F1 Q&A: Monaco sprint, VSc, Russell Spain strategy and having to let multiple drivers past
articles.summary: BBC Sport F1 correspondent Andrew Benson answers your latest questions before the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
articles.body:
Formula 1 has a rare Saturday race this weekend for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Kimi Antonelli goes into round 15 of the season with an imposing 81-point lead in the drivers' championship over Mercedes team-mate George Russell.

BBC F1 correspondent Andrew Benson answers your latest questions before the event in Baku.

What are your thoughts on having a sprint race next year at Monaco? I was very surprised to see that on the calendar, given that the race has so little chance of overtaking - Graham

F1 to have 10 sprint races in 2027, including Monaco

Formula 1 announced the 2027 calendar last week, with the number of sprint events increased from six to 10, and one of them Monaco.

This has proved controversial with some fans.

Why pick the worst track on the calendar for overtaking to have two races in one weekend, some have wondered. What's the point of having two boring races; isn't one enough?

The thinking behind it, though, is less about the races than about qualifying, and how making Monaco a sprint could mix up the weekend.

Monaco qualifying is renowned as one of the highlights of the season. In that case, surely two great qualifying sessions is better than one?

It was also pointed out by F1 that it gives the chance of two different grid orders and therefore more variability.

There is another factor to consider, too.

Monaco is one of the most demanding tracks on the calendar, and it is renowned as somewhere drivers have to build up to the limit progressively so they can become confident with knowing how the car will behave when they get there.

Get that wrong, push too hard too soon, and the chances of an accident are considerably higher.

So asking the drivers to go straight into a qualifying after a single practice session is a really difficult challenge.

It is likely to mean more mistakes, more action, more drama, and therefore more entertainment.

The same goes for grand prix qualifying.

Yes, by then the drivers will have done a sprint race. But there are always changes made to the cars for qualifying, so again the drivers will be going in blind to some degree.

Yes, the sprint is likely to be a procession. How could it be anything else? But it adds an extra degree of jeopardy to the whole weekend.

Do you think F1 might consider the F2 approach for the virtual safety car, where drivers cannot pit under a VSC but can pit under a full safety car? As a regular viewer of both series, I think this works well in F2 and is another way to solve the jeopardy a short VSC period brings to a race. - Caroline

The VSC was discussed at the so-called FIA sporting advisory committee last week, but sources say no consensus emerged there as to potential changes.

It was also on the agenda for the F1 Commission meeting on Monday but there were no significant developments.

Lando Norris, who lost victory in Madrid by the VSC timing, said after the race that the drivers had previously discussed with the FIA the idea that the VSC should be out for a minimum of a lap so this sort of thing could not happen.

But every potential 'solution' comes with consequences. In that case, F1 might end up with a full lap of VSC just to recover a bit of debris.

The VSC was introduced so that relatively small-scale incidents could be dealt with without the lengthy disruption of a full safety car.

It's accepted that the safety car affords possibilities to gain and lose out, so why should the VSC not do the same? The argument is that, generally, these even out over the season, although the Norris case in Madrid had particularly dramatic consequences.

Antonelli benefited from this one, for example, but has lost out in other scenarios this year. For example, when the VSC gifted Lewis Hamilton the lead in Barcelona, even if that was rendered moot by Antonelli's subsequent retirement.

Why did Mercedes put George Russell on a two-stop strategy in the Spanish Grand Prix when the race has the longest pit lane of the season? George was the only driver out of the top 15 finishers on a two-stop and did this decision cost him a podium finish? - Richard

Mercedes were a bit stuck when the virtual safety car was deployed on lap 14 in Madrid.

The team had split the drivers' tyre strategies - Kimi Antonelli took the conventional strategy and started on the mediums, Russell had gone for the hards.

With overtaking so difficult in Madrid, it was always likely that one option would turn out to be sub-optimal. The timing of the VSC was very unfortunate for those who started on hard tyres because it coincided with the pit-stop window for those on mediums.

Mercedes had two choices - stay out, or pit and change tyre compound, as drivers are obligated to use two compounds during a dry grand prix.

Charles Leclerc, who also started on hards and was running immediately ahead of Russell, stayed out. Mercedes pitted in the hope of trying to beat Leclerc.

Whichever tyre Russell chose was unlikely to make it to the end, so Mercedes knew at that point they would almost certainly have to stop again.

The hard tyre was comfortably the best race tyre in Madrid, and on his mediums Russell did not have the pace to narrow the gap to Leclerc to less than it takes to do a pit stop. So there was nothing to lose by pitting again.

Team boss Toto Wolff said: "He said the tyres were not in a great shape, the mediums. We didn't think they would go to the end. (We thought) the better opportunity was not to hang out and wait for a red, but to change the tyres and get on with it."

Russell said: "Maybe I could have stayed out with Leclerc but I would have still finished behind him. Maybe I could have not pitted on to the hard again but everything I would have done would have brought us to the same position."

Live commentary on BBC Radio 5 Live and Sports Extra; live text updates on BBC Sport website and app

During the Madrid race, Max Verstappen was told to hand the place back to Lewis Hamilton. Which he did. However, what would happen if Lewis had fallen maybe two or three cars further back. Does Max still have to hand back the place (and lose places to other cars) or would he just have to take a penalty? - Wayne

The scenario you paint actually happened in Madrid. Verstappen also got ahead of Antonelli on the first lap, so when Red Bull told him to let Hamilton by, he also had to let the Mercedes past.

Shortly after that happened, the message "no further action" was displayed on the timing screens and television coverage over the incident.

That was because Verstappen had given the place back by then. Otherwise, he would have been penalised.

So, yes, if a driver is adjudged to have committed an offence that requires giving the place back, they must do so regardless of whether there are at that point other cars between them.

There are two examples of this from Fernando Alonso's career.

In the 2005 Japanese Grand Prix, he passed Christian Klien's Red Bull by cutting the chicane, let him by again on the straight and then passed him into Turn One.

But race director Charlie Whiting did not notice that Alonso had let Klien back past, and after some discussions with the Renault team, he demanded Alonso cede the position.

That was two laps later, by which time Alonso was seven seconds up the road.

At Silverstone in 2010, Alonso, now at Ferrari, was forced off the track by Robert Kubica when trying an overtaking move at Vale, and ended up passing the Renault driver off the track.

Because he had been forced off, Ferrari decided not to give up the position. But Whiting told them they had to, after discussions with the team.

Problem was, at exactly that point, Kubica pulled into the pits to retire, so Alonso could not give the place back - and he was given a drive-through penalty.

Before he could serve it, there was then a safety-car period which closed up the field. Penalties could not be served under a safety car, so the two situations combined dropped Alonso right to the back of the field. He ended up finishing 14th, which was a costly blow to his title hopes.

articles.title: Por qué la carrera del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán es el sábado: el motivo del cambio de horario
articles.standfirst: Este jueves 24 de septiembre arrancarán los motores en Bakú hasta el sábado 26
articles.summary: Este jueves 24 de septiembre arrancarán los motores en Bakú hasta el sábado 26
articles.body: La Fórmula 1 está de regreso tras un par de semanas de parón desde el Gran Premio de Madrid, con el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán en las míticas calles de Bakú. Uno de los Grandes Premios más esperados del calendario de la Fórmula 1 es, sin lugar a duda, el de Azerbaiyán. Correr entre históricos castillos hacen que le den emoción a las carreras que se disputan en las calles de Bakú. Desde su estreno en 2016 acogiendo el Gran Premio de Europa, este fin de semana el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán arranca, por primera vez, un día antes: el miércoles 23 de septiembre con la rueda de prensa oficial previa al Gran Premio. Por lo tanto, se empezarán a escuchar el rugir de los motores el jueves 24 y hasta el sábado 26, cuando se celebre la carrera del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán. El cambio en los horarios de este Gran Premio está relacionado directamente con el país más que con el campeonato en sí. Mientras que en numerosas ocasiones se ha dado la coincidencia entre el Mundial de MotoGP y el de Fórmula 1, cuyos horarios no se han visto afectados por parte de las 4 ruedas, esta vez esos cambios en la Fórmula 1 son por fuerza de causa mayor. El Día del Recuerdo de Azerbaiyán marca una de las fechas más importantes para el país europeo, cayendo este precisamente el 27 de septiembre. Un día que busca homenajear a las victimas de la Segunda Guerra de Nagorno-Karabaj, comenzada hace casi 6 años ese día, en 2020. Ante esta situación y, al tratarse precisamente de una fecha tan emotiva para los azerbaiyanos, las autoridades, tanto del país como del campeonato, acordaron que se adelantasen los horarios una jornada completa, para así poder tener el domingo 27 de septiembre libre en el país y homenajear a su gente como es debido. Además, no sólo se celebra un día antes sino que, la diferencia horaria modifica nuestros horarios también, los cuales se adelantan un par de horas. La acción por las calles de Bakú comenzarán el jueves 24 a las 10.30 con el Libre 1, seguido del Libre 2 a las 14.00 hora peninsular. Del mismo modo, el viernes 25 se dará comienzo al Libre 3 a las 10.30 y a las 14.00 tendrá lugar la Qualy. Por último, el sábado 26 a las 13.00 se dará el pistoletazo de salida a la carrera del Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán.

articles.title: Mir sigue de baja al no saberse aún qué tiene
articles.standfirst: Tras haberse perdido el Gran Premio de Austria, Joan Mir tampoco participará en el Gran Premio de Japón e Indonesia
articles.summary: Tras haberse perdido el Gran Premio de Austria, Joan Mir tampoco participará en el Gran Premio de Japón e Indonesia
articles.body: El Mundial de MotoGP está a punto de arrancar con su Gira Asiática y Joan Mir vuelve a ser baja perdiéndose los dos primeros Grandes Premios en Japón e Indonesia debido a su condición médica, cuyas causas siguen sin tenerse claras. Tras no poder completar la carrera del Gran Premio de San Marino, Joan Mir no pudo participar en el Gran Premio de Austria ante los síntomas que mostró el piloto mallorquín durante el fin de semana en Misano, los cuales le dejaban sin fuerza y energía. Dichos síntomas han obligado al piloto del Honda HRC Castrol a permanecer en reposo absoluto ante las anomalías presentadas en sus analíticas, cuyas causas son completamente desconocidas, mientras que continúan las pruebas pertinentes para dar con la raíz del malestar de Joan Mir. Tal y como el Doctor Ángel Charte, jefe del equipo médico del campeonato de MotoGP, explica a través de un comunicado de Honda HRC Castrol: "Joan Mir lleva varios meses padeciendo diversos síntomas que afectan a su energía y rendimiento, y cuya gravedad ha aumentado recientemente; por el momento, aún no se ha confirmado la causa. Debido a su persistencia y gravedad, Mir se ha sometido a una serie de pruebas en el Hospital Universitario Dexeus con el objetivo de llegar a un diagnóstico definitivo. A raíz de estos síntomas, la recomendación médica es que guarde reposo absoluto y se someta a diversos tratamientos durante los próximos 15 días. Por consiguiente, le he desaconsejado participar en los Grandes Premios de Japón e Indonesia. Mi equipo seguirá supervisando de cerca su estado". A la espera de ver la evolución del mallorquín, el equipo se plantea una sustitución para ambos Grandes Premios, aunque aún está por saberse. Mientras que en el Gran Premio de San Marino Joan Mir fue sustituido por Takaaki Nakagami tras haber acabado recientemente un Test en Mugello, muy probablemente el japonés podría subirse de nuevo a la RC213V, teniendo en cuenta, en especial, que se trata del Gran Premio de casa. Aún y así, el sustituto de Joan Mir para estos dos próximos Grandes Premios está aún por conocerse, según informan desde el equipo Honda HRC Castrol, donde cuentan con dos semanas para tomar la decisión correcta.

articles.title: Formula 1: Isack Hadjar to return from wrist injury at Azerbaijan Grand Prix
articles.summary: Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar will return at this week's Azerbaijan Grand Prix after missing the past three races with a wrist injury.
articles.body:
Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar will return at this week's Azerbaijan Grand Prix after missing the past three races with a wrist injury.

The 21-year-old Frenchman was replaced by New Zealand's Liam Lawson for races in the Netherlands, Monza and Madrid after injuring his wrist while boxing.

In statement, Red Bull said Hadjar has made a "full recovery" and will replace Lawson for the Grand Prix in Baku, which runs from 24-26 September.

"The team would like to sincerely thank Liam for his professionalism, dedication and hard work over the past three races," Red Bull added.

"Stepping in under challenging circumstances, he delivered some impressive performances and made a valuable contribution to the team."

Lawson, 24, finished seventh in Zandvoort and sixth in Madrid but failed to score a point at Monza after coming 14th.

After being replaced by Hadjar, Lawson will return to Red Bull's junior team Racing Bulls.

Hadjar, who will return to action alongside four-time world champion Max Verstappen, is eighth in the drivers' standings having scored 71 points this season.

articles.body:
Hadjar, who has fared reasonably well in his first season as Max Verstappen's team-mate, was unable to drive at races in the Netherlands, Italy and Spain after sustaining the injury while doing fitness training during Formula 1's summer break in August.

The 21-year-old Frenchman's return to the cockpit will come during Thursday's two practice sessions in Baku, with this weekend's schedule moved a day earlier to avoid a clash with Azerbaijan Remembrance Day.

A team statement released on Tuesday morning said: "Oracle Red Bull Racing is delighted to welcome Isack back this weekend.

"Having made a successful recovery from his wrist injury, Isack will return to action at the Baku City Circuit on Thursday."

Liam Lawson was promoted from Racing Bulls to deputise for Hadjar, with reserve driver Yuki Tsunoda filling the New Zealander's seat at Red Bull's junior squad.

Red Bull added: "The team would like to sincerely thank Liam for his professionalism, dedication and hard work over the past three races.

"Stepping in under challenging circumstances, he delivered some impressive performances and made a valuable contribution to the team. We wish him all the very best as he returns to Visa Cash App Racing Bulls."

Racing Bulls also thanked Tsunoda for his contribution, with the Japanese driver now returning to his role as reserve for both teams.

"Liam returns to VCARB this weekend in Baku, with Isack having made a full recovery from his wrist injury," Racing Bulls said.

"A huge thank you to Yuki for stepping in over the past three races, giving everything for the team and scoring some very valuable points."

Hadjar had delivered a solid first campaign with Red Bull up until suffering the injury, claiming a podium for the team in Monaco.

He remains eighth in the Drivers' Championship but a 23-point deficit to McLaren's Oscar Piastri at the time of his injury has increased to 49 points.

Hadjar was trailing Verstappen by 38 points after the final race before the summer break in Hungary but is now 74 points back from the Dutchman.

articles.title: Hadjar está de vuelta a la F1
articles.standfirst: La dupla Verstappen - Hadjar regresa a la parrilla de la Fórmula 1
articles.summary: La dupla Verstappen - Hadjar regresa a la parrilla de la Fórmula 1
articles.body: La Fórmula 1está de regreso e Isack Hajar con ella. Tras haberse perdido los Grandes Premios de Países Bajos, Italia y España, el piloto francés reaparece en el campeonato al haberse recuperado por completo de su lesión en la muñeca izquierda, la cual se fracturó practicando boxeo a modo de entrenamiento durante el verano. Tal y como hace apenas una semana Laurent Mekies, jefe de equipo de Red Bull Racing, explicó a Sky Sports F1, Hadjar tan solo regresaría si se sentía al 100%, ya que no querían que su impaciencia pudiera retrasar aún más la recuperación del francés. No obstante, aunque su reaparición parecía más que segura, seguía estando ese mínimo interrogante, el cuál han respondido a poco menos de 48 horas de dar comienzo al Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán. Una considerable parte de la espera a su completa recuperación tuvo que ver el 9 veces Campeón del Mundo de Motociclismo, Marc Márquez, quien aconsejó a Isack no precipitarse tras llamar éste al ilerdense buscando opinión al respecto. Por lo tanto, el mismo Menkies afirmó de igual forma a Sky Sports F1 que no había ningún problema en la recuperación de Hadjar y que los tiempos que se estaban tomando eran los adecuados para ese tipo de lesiones, sin forzar absolutamente nada. Tras 3 Grandes Premios compartiendo box con Liam Lawson, el cuatro veces Campeón del Mundo tendrá de regreso a su principal compañero de equipo, haciendo así que el norteamericano regrese a Racing Bulls y, del mismo modo, Yuki Tsunoda a la reserva de Red Bull. Así mismo lo anunciaban desde Red Bull Racing en un comunicado oficial: "Oracle Red Bull Racing se complace en dar la bienvenida a Isack este fin de semana», reza un comunicado emitido por Red Bull este martes. Tras haberse recuperado con éxito de su lesión en la muñeca, Isack volverá a la acción el jueves en el Circuito Urbano de Bakú". Aún y así, desde el equipo inglés sienten un gran agradecimiento hacia Lawson, quien ha tenido grandes actuaciones con el equipo oficial, quedando 7º en Zandvoort y 6º en Madring. Así lo han expresado desde Red Bull Racing a través del comunicado: "El equipo quiere expresar su más sincero agradecimiento a Liam por su profesionalidad, dedicación y esfuerzo durante las últimas tres carreras. A pesar de las difíciles circunstancias, realizó unas actuaciones impresionantes y aportó mucho al equipo. Le deseamos todo lo mejor en su regreso a Visa Cash App Racing Bulls". Por lo tanto, el 6 reemprende así el camino con su Red Bull dispuesto a terminar la temporada de la mejor forma posible y seguir los avances que Red Bull tenga previstos para esta temporada con el fin de mejorar las capacidades del Red Bull de cara al próximo año.

articles.title: "Williams la cagó completamente en invierno"
articles.standfirst: Nico Rosberg comenta la situación que atraviesa Williams
articles.summary: Nico Rosberg comenta la situación que atraviesa Williams
articles.body: El piloto alemán, Campeón del Mundo con Mercedes en 2016, ha criticado duramente la situación que está atravesando Williams, equipo con el que debutó hace 20 años, en 2006. "Como Williams había progresado mucho en 2025, pensábamos que volverían a consolidarse de forma permanente entre los seis primeros, pero ahora han sufrido un retroceso enorme, lo cual es bastante sorprendente", comentaba Rosberg en unas declaraciones a British Sky. Llegan las tan esperadas novedades para Carlos Sainz Jr. al traer en el Gran Premio de Azerbaiyán un coche "prácticamente nuevo", tal y como ha descrito James Vowels, jefe de equipo de Williams F1. No obstante, que se haya tenido que esperar hasta prácticamente final de temporada para ver novedades o cambios mínimos en la escudería británica, sacan a relucir las dificultades que ha tenido el equipo durante la temporada y los errores cometidos ante el cambio de reglamento. Aquellas pequeñas mejoras que parecían haber traído a Madrid durante el Gran Premio de España, no fueron suficientes para los pilotos de Williams, quienes acabaron teniendo unos resultados desastrosos en lo que tendría que haber sido uno de los Grandes Premios más especiales para el madrileño. Por ende, Carlos Sainz Jr. sigue siendo bastante crítico ante la situación de su equipo que, en vez de mejorar de un año para otro, tal y como estaba previsto, y haberse beneficiado del cambio de reglamento, ha empeorado de la peor forma posible. El equipo de Williams se postula actualmente como el 9º equipo clasificado de los 11 en competición, tan solo por delante de Aston Martin y Cadillac. Y es que Sainz apostó en 2025 por Williams tras su marcha de Ferrari, sabiendo que era un coche en evolución y que el cambio de normativa podría beneficiar a un equipo en pleno desarrollo. Sin embargo, la suerte se le ha torcido al madrileño y, lo que comenzó como un cuento de hadas, adaptándose de muy buena forma al Williams y llegando a conseguir dos Pódiums en su primera temporada, en los Grandes Premios de Azerbaiyán y Qatar, ha acabado siendo un laberinto sin salida. Este claro descalabro del equipo inglés no ha pasado desapercibido ante nadie, menos aún ante uno de sus debutantes, Nico Rosberg, quien ha juzgado duramente el camino que está llevando Williams este 2026. Ante British Sky, el Campeón del Mundo 2016 ha resumido así la situación: "Williams la cagó completamente en invierno. Intentaron ser muy ambiciosos en la construcción del chasis, abrir nuevos caminos, ser verdaderamente innovadores. Pero eso salió mal". El alemán no tiene ni un solo calificativo bueno para el nuevo FW48, reprochando duramente el trabajo realizado en el monoplaza, especialmente, en el chasis del nuevo modelo. "Llevan demasiado peso en el coche; 10 kg de peso adicional en este deporte suponen, dependiendo del tipo de circuito, unas tres décimas de segundo por vuelta, lo cual es enorme si se tiene un coche demasiado pesado. Es, sencillamente, demasiado tiempo perdido por vuelta", afirmaba Rosberg. Y es que, a pesar de tener el mejor motor, definitivamente no han dado con la tecla correcta en cuanto a chasis se refiere: "Con un motor Mercedes, no hay excusas en lo que respecta al chasis", sentenciaba el expiloto. Rosberg también criticó la aerodinámica: "Estoy bastante seguro de que la aerodinámica tampoco es precisamente óptima. Así que también tienen que hacer grandes avances en ese aspecto". Suponiendo el gran cariño que procesa el alemán por Williams, ya que fue el equipo con el que debutó en 2006, éste ha mostrado la pena que le produce ver esta situación en el equipo inglés: "Este es también un momento difícil para James Vowles, a quien tengo en gran estima, pero ahora tiene que darle la vuelta a la situación para volver a llevar al equipo por un camino positivo, lo cual no es nada fácil".

articles.title: MotoGP acabará en Valencia en 2027
articles.standfirst: El Mundial confirma su fecha y ya se sabe el inicio y el final
articles.summary: El Mundial confirma su fecha y ya se sabe el inicio y el final
articles.body: El Mundial de MotoGP de 2027 va cogiendo forma. El certamen dará a conocer un calendario provisional este mismo viernes pero, mientras, se van sabiendo algunas de las fechas que lo conformarán. Ya se conocían las de los test de pretemporada de 2027, con ensayos en Sepang (Malasia) y Buriram (Tailandia) y, después, la presentación en Brasil para retornar a Tailandia al comienzo, que está previsto del 5 al 7 de marzo. Ahora, MotoGP ha anunciado que el final de temporada será, cómo no, en el circuito Ricardo Tormo de Cheste, en Valencia, con motivo del Gran Premio de la Comunidad Valenciana. Será del 26 al 29 de noviembre, en una fecha parecida a la de 2026. De hecho, para esta campaña ya hay previstas multitud de actividades para los fans en la ciudad del Turia para acompañar a la actividad en el trazado. Carlos Ezpeleta, adjunto al CEO de MotoGP, exponía su satisfacción por tener un broche de oro en la Comunidad Valenciana. "Pocos lugares captan el espíritu del final de temporada de MotoGP como el circuito Ricardo Tormo. El circuito, la ciudad y los aficionados crean cada año un ambiente verdaderamente especial, lo que lo convierte en el escenario perfecto para cerrar una nueva temporada de competición de primer nivel. Nos complace confirmar a Valencia como sede de la última prueba de la temporada 2027" indicó. Juanfran Pérez Llorca, presidente de la Generalitat valenciana ratificaba su orgullo por la elección. "Excelentes noticias para el circuit Ricardo Tormo y para toda la Comunidad Valenciana. Acoger la última prueba del Campeonato del Mundo de MotoGP es un reconocimiento a los organizadores del evento y a nuestros aficionados, que hacen posible que este Gran Premio siga creciendo año tras año", afirmaba. En el 'paddock' de MotoGP todos están pendientes de si se viajará, finalmente, a Qatar y de qué pasará con esta cita en 2027. Carmelo Ezpeleta dio por casi seguro el viaje este fin de semana en Austria.

articles.title: Madring da las cifras finales de su primera edición
articles.standfirst: Cuando están a punto de salir a la venta las primeras entradas para 2027
articles.summary: Cuando están a punto de salir a la venta las primeras entradas para 2027
articles.body: "No fue solo un Gran Premio. Fue el primero. Y acabamos de escribir la primera página de una nueva historia". Eso comentan desde Madring respecto a la primera edición del Gran Premio de España celebrado hace unos días en el circuito urbano de Madrid. El trazado madrileño ofreció sus primeras cifras oficiales y finales respecto a algunos parámetros y los catalogan como un éxito rotundo. Empezando por la asistencia, los espectadores presentes: En el total del fin de semana fueron 352.618. De ellos, 87.890 el viernes, con motivo de los entrenamientos libres 1 y 2; 122.039 para vivir 'in situ' la jornada del sábado, con los Libres 3 y la sesión de clasificación; y 128.183 en el gran día, el domingo, para la carrera. El reparto de ellos también se hizo público: En las gradas fueron 261.766; en las distintas zonas de hospitality, 38.879 y en el Paddock Club, 15.000. Madring, igualmente, informa 275.000 personas, lo que supone 8 de cada 10 asistentes, lo hicieron en transporte público. De ellos, 168.000 fueron en Metro y 107.000 usaron el Cercanías. Igualmente, se hacen públicos algunos datos de audiencia: 288.000 menciones en redes sociales, 1.551.000 espectadores en televisión en abierto, lo que supuso un 16,9 por ciento de cuota de pantalla, 508.000 nuevos usuarios en la web y 45.000 nuevos seguidores en las redes sociales de la instalación madrileña. Por último, se detalla que hubo 264 zonas de restauración, con hasta 2.100 camareros. Además, 9.184 kilos de excedente de comida se donaron tras el gran premio. Todo con la vista puesta ya en 2027, cuando la carrera se celebrará en unas fechas similares, del 10 al 12 de septiembre. De hecho, las primeras entradas ya se pondrán a la venta en unos días, el 29 de septiembre.

articles.title: Hurricane Fly: Willie Mullins-trained dual Champion Hurdle winner dies aged 22
articles.summary: Willie Mullins' brilliant hurdler Hurricane Fly has passed away at the age of 22; the winner of 22 Grade 1's will be remembered as one of the all-time greats of the National Hunt sphere.
articles.body:
The son of Montjeu proved himself one of the greats of recent National Hunt history, winning the Champion Hurdle at Cheltenham in 2011 and 2013 and the Irish Champion Hurdle five times on the spin between 2011 and 2015.

In total Hurricane Fly won a record breaking 22 Grade One races. He was retired in 2015 after a nine-year career to spend his days alongside other equine greats such as Faugheen, Hardy Eustace and Beef Or Salmon at the Irish National Stud.

Mullins described the superstar hurdler as "awesome" and "one of the biggest legends" to pass through his Closutton yard. Regular jockey Ruby Walsh simply labelled him "the perfect horse" and the best jumper of a hurdle he ever rode.

"He won a record-breaking 22 Grade One races, which was remarkable," Mullins told "He's one of the greatest horses to ever come through our stable. He was a horse who loved a battle and was so brave.

"Ruby was able to stand back anywhere on him and he'd answer. He just put his rivals into trouble. He was such a proper horse. He was awesome, one of the biggest legends ever to come through Closutton."

Walsh, who twice scaled the heights at the Festival on his former partner, said: "Hurricane Fly was a brilliant racehorse but was without doubt the best jumper of a hurdle I ever rode.

"He was incredible, his accuracy, his bravery, the speed at which he could move his feet. He was bombproof, you could ride him down to hurdles like they weren't there because he was going to do the right thing every time.

"He had the engine to go with it. He had speed, class, he stayed and was in my eyes, for a little horse, the perfect horse."

Mullins admitted he paid a visit to see his former stable star and had a chance to say his goodbyes.

"I was lucky enough to visit him today just before the end and met Gail (Carlisle, stable lass) who had popped over to see him as well as she'd heard the news. It was very poignant and we were able to say our goodbyes.

"It's especially poignant following so shortly after the passing of his co-owner Frank Boyd and I'm thinking of his family and George Creighton's family too at this time. Hurricane Fly provided us all with so many wonderful days and memories."

The owners issued a statement which read: "The Boyd and Creighton families are deeply saddened to hear of the passing of Hurricane Fly. He provided us with so many great days and long lasting memories.

"We would like to thank Willie Mullins, Gail Carlisle, Harold Kirk and all the staff at Closutton, as well as the National Stud who provided him with such a happy retirement."
